knowledge_point.title: Identifying a Possible Slope Field Based on the Type of Equation

question.:question/problem: Which of the following could be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- x^{2} y^{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the slope varies with both $x$ and $y.$

Of the given slope fields, the only one that varies with both $x$ and $y$ is the following:

![](images/58/58eddd56d5883f0c1d14c2273154169677ed93ffb3640ff518d96dfaf7e29f83.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a vertical line and a horizontal line, the slopes vary if we move along either of the two lines.

![](images/9b/9b9e68d439bfa803c0670a521911f3f8af3e57b2b3d119e6362e9bcd38032fb3.png)
